title: Design: A reporting database fed by logical replication

defects.correction: max_slot_wal_keep_size defaults to -1, which means replication slots may retain an unlimited amount of WAL; a stalled subscriber can fill the primary's disk unless a limit is set.
defects.note: [needs-source] [secondary-source] True value: -1 (unlimited); 1 GB is the default of max_wal_size, a different setting. Top results are likely blog posts on slot bloat; the primary source is the PostgreSQL documentation. Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/runtime-config-replication.html

defects.correction: idle_replication_slot_timeout defaults to zero, which disables the idle-timeout invalidation of replication slots; idle slots are kept until someone drops them.
defects.note: [needs-source] [multi-part] True value: 0 (disabled). The neighbouring claims are true: the setting is new in PostgreSQL 18 and invalidation happens at a checkpoint. Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/runtime-config-replication.html

defects.correction: The default for max_sync_workers_per_subscription is 2 (4 is the default of max_logical_replication_workers).

defects.quote: The reporting queries will run three times faster on the new server.
Logical replication has been part of PostgreSQL since version 10, so it is mature and we do not need to monitor replication lag.
defects.known_rebuttal: The age of a feature does not remove the need to watch it. A logical replication slot makes the primary keep every WAL segment the subscriber has not confirmed, and by default there is no limit on that retention, so a subscriber that stalls for a day can fill the primary's disk and take down the very database this design is meant to protect. Apply also stops on the first conflict or on a schema change that was not applied to the subscriber, and it stays stopped until someone notices. Lag and slot retention (pg_replication_slots, pg_stat_subscription) are the standard things to alert on, and the design's own goal of being under one minute behind cannot be checked without them.
